title: 3,4-Dihydroxybenzaldehyde Exerts Anti-Alzheimer's Effects by Inhibiting Abeta Protofibril Assembly and Activating Antioxidant Defense Mechanisms.
authors: Zhao, Zhourong; Yang, Lin; Zhang, Zhuo; Song, Jia; Zhang, Chao; Duan, Xiaohua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子DBD抑制Aβ原纤维组装及抗氧化应激的阿尔茨海默病保护作用，对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无AI或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: 3,4-Dihydroxybenzaldehyde (DBD) is a polyphenolic active constituent derived from Gastrodia elata. Its characteristic phenolic structure is associated with diverse bioactivities, such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and cardioprotective effects. However, its role and underlying mechanisms in combating Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain inadequately elucidated. In this study, we employed computational and experimental approaches to investigate the anti-AD effects of DBD. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that DBD binds to Abeta fibrils via pi-pi stacking, hydrophobic interactions, and hydrogen bonds, suggesting its potential to disrupt Abeta fibril stability and thereby inhibit aggregation. In vivo experiments in an AD C. elegans model demonstrated that 2 mM DBD treatment significantly delayed paralysis and extended lifespan. It also improved locomotor activity and pharyngeal pumping rates, while reducing lipofuscin accumulation. These results collectively suggest that DBD promotes healthspan-associated phenotypes. Broad-targeted metabolomics analysis indicated that DBD significantly altered the metabolic profile of the worms. Further mechanistic investigations suggested that the protective effects of DBD are associated with the activation of the DAF-16/FOXO and SKN-1/Nrf2 signaling pathways, accompanied by enhanced resistance to oxidative and thermal stress in nematodes. These findings suggest that DBD exhibits anti-AD potential through multimodal mechanisms, which involve interference with Abeta toxicity and reinforcement of cellular defense. This study supports DBD as a candidate compound and provides a rationale for its further investigation.
abstract_zh: 3,4-二羟基苯甲醛（DBD）是从天麻中提取的一种多酚类活性成分。其特有的酚类结构与其多种生物活性相关，如抗炎、抗氧化和心脏保护作用。然而，其在对抗阿尔茨海默病（AD）中的作用及潜在机制尚未得到充分阐明。在本研究中，我们采用计算和实验方法探讨了DBD的抗AD效应。分子动力学模拟显示，DBD通过π-π堆积、疏水相互作用和氢键与Aβ纤维结合，表明其可能破坏Aβ纤维的稳定性，从而抑制聚集。在AD线虫模型的体内实验中，2 mM DBD处理显著延缓了瘫痪并延长了寿命。它还改善了运动活性和咽部泵送速率，同时减少了脂褐素积累。这些结果共同表明，DBD促进了与健康寿命相关的表型。广靶代谢组学分析显示，DBD显著改变了线虫的代谢谱。进一步的机制研究表明，DBD的保护作用与DAF-16/FOXO和SKN-1/Nrf2信号通路的激活相关，并伴随线虫对氧化和热应激抵抗力的增强。这些发现表明，DBD通过多模式机制展现出抗AD潜力，涉及干扰Aβ毒性和增强细胞防御。本研究支持DBD作为候选化合物，并为其进一步研究提供了依据。
